clue.text: The wild southerly winds blew

indicators.note: winds as a verb means twists about, so the letters before it are twisted into a new order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south, so southerly gives S

explanation.surface: A report on wild winds from the south that blew across the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' looks like the subject of 'blew' but is the anagram signal: THE WILD plus S is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Whistled means made a shrill sound by forcing air out, which is what a wind that blew hard does.

clue.text: Fried dish cook made with a pan

indicators.note: to cook something up is to concoct it, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe note: fry this dish using a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cook' reads as a kitchen instruction but is the anagram signal: MADE plus A PAN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An empanada is a Spanish or Latin American pastry turnover, often fried, so a fried dish.

clue.text: Note beer leads to depression

parts.note: D is one of the musical notes of the scale
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Beer drinking leads to a low mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' reads as gloom after drink, but it means a hollow in the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A dale is a valley, a low-lying hollow in hill country, which is a depression in the ground.

clue.text: Obsolete component leading to misaligned tape

parts.note: passé means out of date or obsolete
a part is a component of something
out, as in out of true, means misaligned

explanation.surface: An outdated component is why the tape went crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading to' is a link joining the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Passe-partout is an adhesive tape used for binding the edges of a framed picture to its glass.

clue.text: Bad temper witnessed about parking by learner

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for witnessed goes around the next letters

parts.note: seen means witnessed
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered scene witnessed in a car park with a learner driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts P and L inside SEEN, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Spleen is a figurative word for ill humour or anger, once thought to come from that organ.

clue.text: Tin fruit shortly before start of autumn to generate capital

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the fruit word loses its last letter

parts.note: a berry is a fruit

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Canning fruit before autumn to raise money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts BERRY to BERR. 'capital' suggests money but means a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Canberra is the capital city of Australia.

clue.text: Deliberately contrived to stop working when crossed by boss

indicators.note: crossed by means having something run through it, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a raised ornamental knob
a machine that dies stops working

explanation.surface: Someone deliberately downs tools when the boss crosses them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' suggests a manager, but here it is the raised ornamental knob; 'when crossed by' signals one piece running through the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A studied manner is one that is deliberate and contrived rather than natural.

clue.text: Spacecraft puts in orbit family from the east

indicators.note: in orbit means circling round, so these letters are spun into a new order
in an across clue, read from the east means read from right to left, so backwards

parts.note: kin means family

explanation.surface: A spacecraft puts a family from the east into orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in orbit' rearranges PUTS into SPUT; 'from the east' turns KIN into NIK.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputnik was the Soviet satellite, the first spacecraft put into Earth orbit, in 1957.

clue.text: Security barrier is rubbish — with infra-red included

indicators.note: included means put inside, so the other letters go within the word for rubbish

parts.note: tripe means rubbish or nonsense

explanation.surface: A security barrier dismissed as rubbish, even with infra-red sensors built in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included' signals insertion; 'barrier' suggests a fence, but the answer is a hidden wire that trips an alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripwire is a wire stretched low that sets off an alarm or trap, a security device.

clue.text: Kill vacant time with a drink

parts.note: to ice someone is slang for to kill them

indicators.note: vacant means emptied of its inside, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Killing time with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant' empties TIME to TE. ICE meaning kill is American slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice tea, more often iced tea, is a cold drink of chilled tea.

clue.text: Sleuth or agent visit upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A detective or agent's visit is overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges all twelve letters of OR AGENT VISIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An investigator, such as a private eye, is a sleuth who looks into cases.

clue.text: Corn, perhaps drawing out a broad smile

indicators.note: drawing out means pulling out, so the letter A is removed from the word

parts.note: corn is an example of grain, flagged by perhaps

explanation.surface: Drawing out a broad smile with corn, perhaps a corny joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing out a' takes the A from GRAIN; 'drawing out' might suggest lengthening, but it means extracting.
explanation.definitionFit: A grin is a wide smile showing the teeth.

clue.text: Fiddled, endlessly accompanying tea dance

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: endlessly means losing the end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: conned means swindled, as fiddled does

explanation.surface: A fiddler plays on and on to accompany a tea dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddled' suggests playing a violin but means swindled, CONNED, which 'endlessly' cuts to CONNE. 'accompanying' joins it to CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaconne is a slow stately dance in triple time, and music written for it.

clue.text: Go off romantic engagement round school

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the date word goes around the school

parts.note: a date is a romantic appointment
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A romantic engagement goes off near a school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' signals the container; Eton College is a famous English boarding school, a common crossword school.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate is to explode, which is what a bomb does when it goes off.

clue.text: Osteopath working, but not over sensitive area

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: An osteopath at work avoids going over a sensitive spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not over' takes one O out of OSTEOPATH; 'working' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat spot is a small red spot on the skin, a point especially sensitive to heat.

clue.text: Seen mostly going after tender mince cooked with potatoes

indicators.note: going after means coming next in order, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: to tend sheep is a shepherd's work, so a tender is a shepherd

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: spied means seen

explanation.surface: A recipe: seen mostly after tender mince is cooked with potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' suggests soft meat but means one who tends, a SHEPHERD; 'mostly' cuts SPIED to SPIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Shepherd's pie is a British dish of minced lamb topped with mashed potato.

clue.text: Swiss city girl found beheaded in country road

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the shortened name goes within the road

parts.note: a lane is a narrow country road

indicators.note: beheaded means losing the first letter

parts.note: Susan is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl found headless on a country road in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' drops the girl's first letter, and 'in' places what is left inside the road, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lausanne is a city in Switzerland on Lake Geneva.

clue.text: Marshland about to cut river protection

indicators.note: to cut means to slice into, so the letters go inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a fen is low marshy land
C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Marshland is about to cut off a river's protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' signals insertion; the Dee is a river flowing through Wales, England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Defence means protection from attack.

clue.text: Turner's motion involving artist causes wrench

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the spin goes around the artist

parts.note: a turner's motion is a turn, a spin
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: The painter Turner's movement involves an artist and causes an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter J M W Turner, but here it is anything that turns; 'involving' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprain is a twisting injury to a joint, also called a wrench.

clue.text: Cordelia? Goneril? See a bad character there

indicators.note: see means look inside the words that precede, where the letters lie

explanation.surface: Looking at King Lear's daughters, one sees a bad character there.
explanation.walkthrough: Cordelia and Goneril are daughters in Shakespeare's King Lear; the villain spans their names, CordelIA GOneril, from another Shakespeare play.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is the villain of Shakespeare's Othello, a famously bad character.

clue.text: Style of car in fashion again with leading fleet

indicators.note: leading means going first, so the word for fleet comes in front

parts.note: fleet means swift or fast
back in fashion means popular again

explanation.surface: A car style is back in fashion, with the fleet leading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleet' suggests a group of cars but means quick.
explanation.definitionFit: A fastback is a car whose roof slopes in one line down to the rear.

clue.text: Screen instrument where doctors are operating on heart, perhaps

parts.note: an operating theatre is where surgeons work
the heart is an example of an organ, flagged by perhaps

explanation.surface: Doctors are operating on a heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' means the cinema screen: a theatre organ played in cinemas between films.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre organ is a pipe organ built for cinemas, an instrument of the silver-screen era.

clue.text: Formal speech placed before queen, perhaps

parts.note: set means placed
a queen is an example of a chess piece

explanation.surface: A formal speech placed before the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queen' suggests the monarch but is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A set piece is a prepared, formally composed passage such as a rehearsed speech.

clue.text: Direct attention to head, openly gay

parts.note: a point is a head, as of a pin or headland
out means openly gay

explanation.surface: Drawing attention to someone at the top who is openly gay.
explanation.definitionFit: To point out is to indicate, to draw attention to something.

clue.text: Visionary concept placed on record

parts.note: an idea is a concept
a list is a written record

explanation.surface: A visionary concept is placed on record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed on' is a link: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist is a visionary, someone guided by ideals rather than practicalities.

clue.text: Fake iron caught fire — it needs binning

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: needs binning means is to be thrown away, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: ignited means caught fire
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fake iron caught fire and needs throwing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it needs binning' takes IT out of IGNITED, leaving IGNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Feigned means pretended or faked.

clue.text: I mind about new plan

indicators.note: about means around, so the letters for I and mind go around the letter for new

parts.note: to tend is to mind or look after

explanation.surface: I mind a new plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N between I and TEND.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend is to plan or mean to do something.

clue.text: Number killed off by corrupted meat

indicators.note: killed off means removed, so the letter is taken out of the word for corrupted

parts.note: venal means corrupt, open to bribery

explanation.surface: Someone killed off by corrupted meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a count, but it is the abbreviation N, removed from VENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Veal is the meat of a calf.
